research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only: direct official DESNZ, Ofgem, NESO, Environment Agency, Ofwat, DfT, Ofcom and BDUK verification; 2026 currentness where available; connection-offer/queue, capacity, wayleave/land-right, water-resource/new-connection, street-works, broadband-coverage and planned-deployment separation. Not parcel-level utility availability or capacity.

verification.method: Direct official-web verification plus repository duplicate searches

official_sources.name: Electricity network infrastructure consents land access and rights consultation
official_sources.fact: Updated 27 April 2026; DESNZ covers necessary wayleaves, substation permitted development, section 37 overhead-line consent, private streets and access rights.
official_sources.gate: Policy or a statutory route is not proof that exact land rights, consent or access have been secured for a parcel.

official_sources.name: Electricity network infrastructure land rights government response
official_sources.fact: Updated 27 April 2026; government response explains existing voluntary and compulsory land-right routes and reforms for electricity infrastructure.
official_sources.gate: A reform decision does not establish an operative wayleave, easement, CPO or access right on a target site.

official_sources.name: Ofgem demand connections reform
official_sources.fact: Published 13 February 2026 with response summary added 16 June 2026; Ofgem is developing reforms to curate and prioritise the growing demand-connections queue.
official_sources.gate: Policy options or response analysis are not final connection offers, capacity reservations or parcel-specific connection dates.

official_sources.name: Ofgem Connect update demand connections reform
official_sources.fact: Published 16 June 2026; Ofgem describes the Connect pillar and constraints affecting viable demand projects awaiting electricity connections.
official_sources.gate: A system-level reform update is not evidence that a site has a viable connection point, date or network capacity.

official_sources.name: Ofgem connections reform and battery capacity update
official_sources.fact: Published 17 April 2026; DESNZ and Ofgem report on connections-reform delivery and battery-storage queue issues.
official_sources.gate: Queue reform progress or technology oversupply is not a parcel-specific grid-capacity or consent conclusion.

official_sources.name: Ofgem Gate 2 to Whole Queue timetable decision
official_sources.fact: Published 3 June 2026; Ofgem agreed phased milestones for Gate 2 connection offers through 2026 into March 2027.
official_sources.gate: A programme timetable is not an issued, accepted or technically deliverable offer for an individual project.

official_sources.name: Ofgem find energy supplier or network operator
official_sources.fact: Ofgem directs customers needing a mains connection to the relevant electricity or gas network operator.
official_sources.gate: Identifying the operator does not prove spare capacity, connection cost, route, land rights or delivery date.

official_sources.name: Ofgem Guaranteed Standards of Performance 2026
official_sources.fact: Published 13 March 2026; Ofgem sets 2026-27 electricity-distribution guaranteed-standard payment amounts, including connection standards.
official_sources.gate: A service standard or compensation regime is not proof that a requested connection is technically feasible or available by a target date.

official_sources.name: NESO About Connections Reform
official_sources.fact: NESO explains Gate 1 and Gate 2 criteria, readiness and strategic alignment in the reformed connections process.
official_sources.gate: Gate status is a queue/contract state and must not be converted into planning permission, energisation or parcel-level capacity.

official_sources.name: NESO connections reform timeline
official_sources.fact: NESO publishes phased offer windows for protected, Gate 2 Phase 1 and Gate 2 Phase 2 transmission and distribution projects.
official_sources.gate: Published windows are programme targets, not guaranteed individual offer or energisation dates.

official_sources.name: NESO Transmission Entry Capacity register
official_sources.fact: NESO publishes a twice-weekly TEC register for contracted existing and future projects, including Gate classification fields under Connections Reform.
official_sources.gate: A TEC-register entry is not evidence of construction, energisation, local distribution capacity or exact parcel connection feasibility.

official_sources.name: NESO connections reports and registers
official_sources.fact: NESO states its connections registers show the latest contracted position and are updated twice weekly.
official_sources.gate: Register discovery or contract status does not establish project delivery, planning status or spare capacity for another site.

official_sources.name: NESO readiness declaration template
official_sources.fact: Gate 2 applicants must provide evidence against readiness criteria and strategic alignment through the prescribed process.
official_sources.gate: Submission or claimed readiness is not a Gate 2 award, signed offer or energised connection.

official_sources.name: NESO increasing transparency on connections offers
official_sources.fact: Published 8 April 2026; NESO reports progress in issuing protected Gate 2 offers and development of cross-industry progress visibility.
official_sources.gate: Aggregate offer progress is not evidence of an individual project's signed offer, completion date or grid availability.

official_sources.name: NESO understanding your offer and support
official_sources.fact: NESO guidance covers offer signing deadlines and 2026 modification-scoping support for customers receiving Gate 2 outcomes/offers.
official_sources.gate: Receiving a notification or offer is not equivalent to acceptance, construction, energisation or immutable connection terms.

official_sources.name: NESO high-voltage Gate 2 Phase 2 demand information request
official_sources.fact: The 2026 process states any future high-voltage offer, location and date depend on NGET assessment and engineering studies.
official_sources.gate: Expression of interest or qualification is not a connection offer, selected location or confirmed capacity.

official_sources.name: NESO Material Technology Change Guidance
official_sources.fact: NESO distinguishes material technology changes under enduring connections reform from the Gate 2 to Whole Queue process.
official_sources.gate: A permissible modification route does not prove revised capacity, queue position or delivery without an accepted contract change.

official_sources.name: NESO Gated Modification Guidance
official_sources.fact: NESO guidance explains which modification applications are gated and must use specified application windows.
official_sources.gate: Eligibility to submit a modification is not approval of revised connection terms or capacity.

official_sources.name: Water resources planning guideline
official_sources.fact: Updated 16 June 2026; the Environment Agency, NRW and Ofwat guideline sets how water companies plan secure supply, demand, uncertainty and options through WRMPs.
official_sources.gate: A regional/company WRMP is strategic supply planning and is not proof of an individual development's available connection capacity.

official_sources.name: Water resources planning guideline update outcome
official_sources.fact: Updated 8 May 2026; the Environment Agency confirms consultation changes supporting secure water supplies and environmental protection.
official_sources.gate: Guidance adoption does not itself allocate water capacity or grant connection rights to a parcel.

official_sources.name: Ofwat new connections
official_sources.fact: Ofwat explains new-connection markets and water/sewerage companies' duties to develop networks for growth under sections 37 and 94 of the Water Industry Act 1991.
official_sources.gate: A general statutory duty to develop networks is not proof of immediate local capacity, connection route or development viability.

official_sources.name: Ofwat charging rules overview
official_sources.fact: Ofwat describes developer/new-connection charging rules and changes taking effect from 1 April 2026.
official_sources.gate: A charging framework or worked example is not a site-specific quotation, capacity reservation or connection agreement.

official_sources.name: Ofwat April 2026 English new connection rules
official_sources.fact: The rules govern how English undertakers set and explain charges for new connection services from April 2026.
official_sources.gate: Compliance with charging rules does not demonstrate physical network capacity or an accepted connection design.

official_sources.name: Ofwat bulk charges for new appointments decision
official_sources.fact: Published 7 November 2025; Ofwat issued rules for bulk supply/discharge charges to new appointees taking effect from April 2026.
official_sources.gate: Bulk-charge rules are regulatory terms, not proof that a particular NAV or development has secured bulk capacity.

official_sources.name: Ofwat charging rules history
official_sources.fact: Ofwat records the issue history and effective dates of connection and bulk-charging rules, including the April 2026 regime.
official_sources.gate: Historical/current rule provenance must not be confused with a company-specific quote, agreement or capacity position.

official_sources.name: Ofwat measures of experience
official_sources.fact: Ofwat's 2025-30 D-MeX framework measures water-company service to developer-services customers including new connections.
official_sources.gate: Service-performance metrics are not engineering-capacity metrics and cannot prove a site's connection feasibility.

official_sources.name: Ofwat measures of experience 2025-2030
official_sources.fact: The 2025-30 D-MeX combines developer satisfaction and levels-of-service metrics for developer-service transactions.
official_sources.gate: A high service score does not imply spare water/sewer capacity, approval or a faster exact-site connection.

official_sources.name: Ofwat C-MeX and D-MeX 2024-25 results
official_sources.fact: Ofwat publishes company-level developer-service performance results for 2024-25.
official_sources.gate: Historical company service ranking is not a parcel-level capacity, cost or connection-date forecast.

official_sources.name: Ofwat Direct Procurement for Customers guidance v2
official_sources.fact: Published 26 May 2026; Ofwat guidance sets regulatory/commercial expectations for major water-company projects delivered through DPC.
official_sources.gate: A major-project procurement route is not evidence that local network reinforcement serving a target development is funded or delivered.

official_sources.name: Ofwat PR24 Delivery Plans assessment framework
official_sources.fact: Published 14 May 2026; Ofwat describes monitoring of water-company delivery plans under the 2025-30 investment programme.
official_sources.gate: Company investment plans and monitoring do not prove exact local reinforcement timing or development connection capacity.

official_sources.name: DfT street works permit schemes
official_sources.fact: Updated 19 March 2026 and applying from 10 April 2026; statutory guidance governs highway-authority permit schemes for street works.
official_sources.gate: A permit scheme or eligibility to apply is not an issued permit, apparatus right, land right or utility connection approval.

official_sources.name: DfT co-ordinating street works
official_sources.fact: The March 2026 code applies from 10 April 2026 and covers authority/undertaker coordination duties under NRSWA.
official_sources.gate: Coordination duties do not establish a utility's right to occupy exact land, approved route or connection availability.

official_sources.name: DfT Plan and manage roadworks Street Manager
official_sources.fact: Street Manager is used by highway authorities, utilities and contractors to apply for permits and record street/road works in England.
official_sources.gate: A Street Manager record is works-process evidence, not proof of utility capacity, completion, energisation or permanent rights.

official_sources.name: DfT street works permit scheme conditions
official_sources.fact: Updated December 2025 and effective 5 January 2026; statutory guidance defines conditions authorities may attach to street-work permits.
official_sources.gate: Permit conditions regulate works execution and do not themselves grant a utility connection or property right.

official_sources.name: Ofcom Connected Nations Spring 2026
official_sources.fact: Published 13 May 2026; Ofcom reports fixed broadband and mobile coverage snapshots using data as of January 2026.
official_sources.gate: Area/premises coverage statistics are not a guaranteed service level, install date or exact-site business-grade connectivity result.

official_sources.name: Ofcom Planned Network Deployments 2026
official_sources.fact: Published 13 May 2026; Ofcom reports operator plans for very-high-capacity fixed networks through January 2029, including confidence criteria.
official_sources.gate: Planned/high-confidence deployment is not completed build, premises serviceability or a contractual delivery commitment.

official_sources.name: Ofcom broadband and mobile coverage checker
official_sources.fact: Ofcom's checker provides postcode-level broadband availability and predicted mobile coverage and explicitly does not report current network faults.
official_sources.gate: Checker availability/prediction is not a site survey, guaranteed speed, leased-line capacity or installation commitment.

official_sources.name: Ofcom Electronic Communications Code template notices
official_sources.fact: Ofcom explains Code-operator rights to install/maintain apparatus and prescribed notices used in specified Code processes.
official_sources.gate: Code powers or service of a notice do not prove an agreement, court-imposed right, planning compliance or completed apparatus installation.

official_sources.name: Ofcom private land access code of practice
official_sources.fact: Ofcom's code of practice supports negotiations between Code operators and landowners for access to private land.
official_sources.gate: Best-practice negotiation guidance is not a granted Code right, wayleave, lease or compulsory court order.

official_sources.name: BDUK July 2026 Project Gigabit contract progress
official_sources.fact: Updated 20 July 2026; BDUK publishes contract-level premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit and notes scope/data-timing limitations.
official_sources.gate: Contracted/built programme counts are not proof that an exact parcel is serviceable, scheduled or covered by a supplier commitment.
